docs.title: Drilling Optimization
docs.text: Real-time ROP prediction and torque/vibration monitoring for drilling operations optimization.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: This machine learning system is part of the Oil & Gas ML Portfolio by Kelvin J Cabrera.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text: Synthetic Data Generator -> Scikit-Learn Training -> Flask API -> Streamlit Dashboard

docs.title: Key Features
docs.text:
• Data Generation: Domain-aware synthetic data with physical correlations
  • Model Training: Scikit-learn pipelines (Random Forest, Isolation Forest) with MLflow tracking
  • API: Flask/FastAPI with API key authentication
  • Dashboard: Streamlit interactive web interface
  • Testing: pytest with model evaluation metrics (R2, accuracy, F1)

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
pip install -r requirements.txt
python train.py
python app.py
streamlit run streamlit_app.py

docs.title: API Endpoints
docs.text:
Method Endpoint Description GET / Service info and available models POST /predict/{model} Run inference (requires API key)

Authentication

All API endpoints require an X-API-Key header. Set API_KEY in your environment.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
All API requests require an API key sent via the X-API-Key header.

import requests

headers = {"X-API-Key": "your-api-key"}
response = requests.post("http://localhost:5000/predict/model", json={...}, headers=headers)

docs.title: GET /
docs.text:
Returns service information and available models.

Response:

{"service": "Drilling Optimization", "models": ["model1", "model2"]}

docs.title: POST /predict/{model_name}
docs.text:
Run inference on a trained model.

Request Body:

{"features": {"feature_1": 0.5, "feature_2": 1.2}}

Response:

{"prediction": 0.85, "model": "model_name"}

docs.title: Error Codes
docs.text: Code Description 401 Invalid or missing API key 404 Model not found 422 Invalid input format

docs.title: Data Layer
docs.text:
• Data Source: Synthetic drilling data generator (DrillingDataGenerator) producing 5000 records
  • Formations: arena (sand), caliza (limestone), lutita (shale), dolomita (dolomite)
  • Bit Types: polycrystalline, roller_cone, pdc
  • Preprocessing: One-hot encoding for categorical features, standard scaling

docs.title: ROP Predictor
docs.text:
• Algorithm: GradientBoosting (best) among Random Forest, ExtraTrees, SVR, MLP
  • Target: Rate of Penetration (ft/hr)
  • Features: depth, WOB, RPM, flow rate, mud weight, formation, bit type, bit diameter, mud viscosity, hydraulic pressure
  • Metrics: R2, MAE, MAPE

docs.title: Torque Predictor
docs.text:
• Algorithm: GradientBoosting (best)
  • Target: Drilling torque (klft)
  • Same features as ROP
  • Metrics: R2, MAE, MAPE

docs.title: Vibration Analyzer
docs.text:
• Algorithm: Dual-purpose model
  • Classification: Vibration severity level (low/medium/high/critical)
  • Regression: Continuous vibration value (g)
  • Features: Same drilling parameters
  • Metrics: Classification accuracy, Regression R2

docs.title: Optimization Engine
docs.text:
• Method: Grid search over WOB (10-30 klbf) and RPM (80-140)
  • Objective: Maximize predicted ROP
  • Constraint: Vibration < 2.5 g (safe operating limit)
  • Output: Optimal WOB, RPM, predicted ROP and torque

docs.title: API Layer
docs.text:
• Framework: Flask
  • Endpoints: 5 REST endpoints (health, models, predict, optimize, docs)
  • Model Loading: Lazy loading with pickle deserialization

docs.title: Dashboard Layer
docs.text:
• Frontend: Flask + HTML/CSS/JS
  • Charts: Drilling parameter visualizations, optimization results

docs.title: Data Flow
docs.text:
1. Input: Drilling parameters (depth, WOB, RPM, mud properties, formation, bit)
  2. Preprocessing: DrillingPreprocessor encodes categoricals and scales numerics
  3. Prediction: Three models predict ROP, torque, and vibration simultaneously
  4. Optimization: Grid search finds optimal WOB/RPM combinations
  5. Response: Predicted values and optimal parameters returned as JSON

docs.title: Training Pipeline
docs.text:
1. Generate synthetic drilling data (5000 records)
  2. Preprocess with encoding and scaling
  3. Split 80/20 train/test
  4. Train ROP, Torque, and Vibration models
  5. Evaluate each model (R2, MAE, MAPE, Accuracy)
  6. Save models and preprocessor to outputs/models/

docs.title: File Structure
docs.text:
drilling-optimization/
├── drilling_optimization/
│   ├── data_generator.py       # Synthetic drilling data
│   ├── models/

docs.title: Dockerfile
docs.text:
FROM python:3.10-slim

WORKDIR /app

COPY requirements.txt .
RUN pip install --no-cache-dir -r requirements.txt

COPY . .

RUN python train.py

EXPOSE 5004

CMD ["python", "app.py"]

docs.title: Build and Run
docs.text:
docker build -t drilling-optimization .
docker run -p 5004:5004 drilling-optimization

docs.title: Docker Compose
docs.text:
version: '3.8'
services:
  app:
    build: .
    ports:
      - "5004:5004"
    environment:
      - FLASK_DEBUG=0
    volumes:
      - ./outputs:/app/outputs
    restart: unless-stopped

docker-compose up -d

docs.title: Security
docs.text:
• Set DEBUG=False in production
  • Use HTTPS with a reverse proxy
  • Validate drilling parameter ranges
  • Add rate limiting on optimization endpoint

docs.title: Monitoring
docs.text:
• Monitor /api/health for uptime
  • Log optimization requests and results
  • Track ROP predictions vs actuals for model drift

docs.title: Performance
docs.text:
• Optimization endpoint performs grid search (60 combinations per request)
  • Consider caching results for repeated formations
  • Pre-load models at startup

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Machine Learning system for oil drilling parameter optimization. Predicts Rate of Penetration (ROP), drilling torque, and vibration severity. Automatically optimizes WOB and RPM for maximum drilling efficiency with safe vibration levels.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Python 3.8+
  • pip

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/kcabrera83/drilling-optimization.git
cd drilling-optimization
pip install -r requirements.txt

docs.title: Training Models
docs.text:
python train.py

Generates 5000 synthetic drilling records, trains 3 models, saves to outputs/models/.

docs.title: Starting the Server
docs.text:
python app.py

Open http://localhost:5004 in your browser.

docs.title: Dashboard Features
docs.text:
• Drilling Prediction: Input drilling parameters and get ROP, torque, and vibration predictions
  • Parameter Optimization: Automatically find optimal WOB and RPM for maximum ROP
  • Model Information: View trained model details and performance metrics
  • Interactive Forms: Real-time prediction with validation

docs.title: Input Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Unit Description depth_m m Well depth wob_klbf klbf Weight on bit rpm RPM Rotation speed flow_rate_gpm GPM Mud flow rate mud_weight_ppg ppg Mud density formation - Rock type (arena, caliza, lutita, dolomita) bit_type - Drill bit type (polycrystalline, roller_cone, pdc) bit_diameter_in in Bit diameter mud_viscosity_cp cP Mud viscosity hyd_pressure_psi psi Hydraulic pressure

docs.title: Output Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Unit Description rop_ft_hr ft/hr Rate of penetration torque_klft klft Drilling torque vibration_g g Vibration acceleration vibration_severity - low / medium / high / critical

docs.title: Using curl
docs.text:
# Predict drilling parameters
curl -X POST http://localhost:5004/api/predict \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "depth_m": 2000,
    "wob_klbf": 20,
    "rpm": 120,
    "flow_rate_gpm": 500,
    "mud_weight_ppg": 10.5,
    "formation": "arena",
    "bit_type": "polycrystalline",
    "bit_diameter_in": 12.25
  }'

# Optimize drilling parameters
curl -X POST http://localhost:5004/api/optimize \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "depth_m": 2000,
    "flow_rate_gpm": 500,
    "mud_weight_ppg": 10.5,
    "formation": "arena"
  }'

# Get model info
curl http://localhost:5004/api/models

docs.title: Using Python
docs.text:
import requests

# Predict drilling parameters
response = requests.post("http://localhost:5004/api/predict", json={
    "depth_m": 2000, "wob_klbf": 20, "rpm": 120,
    "flow_rate_gpm": 500, "mud_weight_ppg": 10.5,
    "formation": "arena", "bit_type": "polycrystalline"
})
result = response.json()
print(f"ROP: {result['rop_ft_hr']} ft/hr")
print(f"Torque: {result['torque_klft']} klft")
print(f"Vibration: {result['vibration_g']} g ({result['vibration_severity']})")

# Optimize parameters
response = requests.post("http://localhost:5004/api/optimize", json={
    "depth_m": 2000, "flow_rate_gpm": 500,
    "mud_weight_ppg": 10.5, "formation": "arena"
})
opt = response.json()
print(f"Optimal WOB: {opt['optimal_wob']} klbf, RPM: {opt['optimal_rpm']}")

docs.title: Training Results
docs.text:
• Dataset: 5000 synthetic drilling records
  • ROP Predictor: GradientBoosting (R2 > 0.95)
  • Torque Predictor: GradientBoosting (R2 > 0.95)
  • Vibration Analyzer: Classification + regression (Accuracy > 0.90)

docs.title: Training Pipeline
docs.text:
The training pipeline follows these steps:

  1. Data Generation: data_generator.py creates synthetic data with domain-specific physical correlations
  2. Preprocessing: Feature scaling via StandardScaler
  3. Training: Random Forest or Isolation Forest via scikit-learn
  4. Evaluation: R2 score, accuracy, classification report
  5. Logging: MLflow tracks parameters, metrics, and artifacts
  6. Serialization: Model + scaler + metadata saved as .pkl via joblib

docs.title: Model Files
docs.text:
Models are stored in outputs/models/*.pkl as dictionaries with:

Key Description model Trained scikit-learn estimator scaler Fitted StandardScaler feature_names List of input feature names target_name Target variable name metrics Evaluation metrics from training

docs.title: Retraining
docs.text:
To retrain:

python train.py

This will update the model files in outputs/models/ and log results to MLflow.
